clue.text: Tax guide for one involved in aeronautics research

parts.note: to tax someone is to strain or test them
a pilot guides a ship into harbour

explanation.surface: Someone helps a researcher in aeronautics fill in a tax return.
explanation.definitionFit: A test pilot flies experimental aircraft, so their work is part of aeronautical research and development.

clue.text: Nasty creature appears in this half-light

indicators.note: the creature appears in, i.e. is placed inside, the other piece
half of the four-letter word this means only its first two letters are used

parts.note: an orc is a monstrous creature in Tolkien and fantasy fiction

explanation.surface: A monster lurks in the dim twilight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-light' reads as twilight, but 'half' acts on 'this' to give TH, and 'light' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A torch is a portable lamp, a source of illumination carried in the hand.

clue.text: Republican abandons unusually strong view — a potential election winner

indicators.note: the remaining letters are arranged in an unusual order
the Republican abandons the phrase, so that letter leaves the fodder

explanation.surface: A Republican drops a firmly held opinion, which might win an election.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandons' removes R from STRONG VIEW, and 'unusually' rearranges the remaining nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A swing vote is the ballot of an undecided voter, which can tip a close contest one way.

clue.text: Paper supplier appears as crowd stop working

parts.note: a press is a dense crowd of people
to bar is to stop or block
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: A stationery supplier seems to be a crowd that has downed tools.
explanation.definitionFit: A press baron owns newspapers, so he supplies papers in the journalistic sense.

clue.text: Miss an opportunity to make couture restorative

parts.note: read as an instruction, the answer says drop the letters O, U, T, which turns couture into cure, a restorative

explanation.surface: Someone misses a chance by trying to make high fashion healing.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half is the answer read as an instruction: remove OUT from COUTURE and CURE, a restorative, is left.
explanation.definitionFit: To lose out is to fail to benefit from a chance others have taken.

clue.text: Informed about English National Front showing large increase

indicators.note: the word for informed goes about, or around, the other pieces

parts.note: to have told someone is to have informed them
NF is the abbreviation for the National Front, a British far-right party

explanation.surface: Someone is told that a far-right party's support has grown greatly.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenfold means multiplied by ten, a large rise in amount.

clue.text: Plot to snaffle small change, so unlike Long John Silver

indicators.note: to snaffle is to grab, so the plot takes the change inside it

parts.note: a bed is a plot in a garden
1p, one penny, is small change; read as letters it looks like IP

explanation.surface: A scheme to pinch coins, quite unlike the scheming pirate of Treasure Island.
explanation.walkthrough: '1p' (one penny) is written with the digit 1 read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Long John Silver has one leg; a biped walks on two, so it is unlike him.

clue.text: Produce from central Umbria and Oviedo

indicators.note: central picks the middle two letters of each of the two place names

explanation.surface: Farm goods come from the heart of an Italian and a Spanish region.
explanation.definitionFit: Brie is a French cheese, a dairy product or item of farm produce.

clue.text: Socialist has fix on how fight can be ended

parts.note: to pin something is to fix it in place
KO, a knockout, ends a boxing match

explanation.surface: A left-winger arranges how a boxing bout will finish.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinko is a derogatory slang term for someone with left-wing views.

clue.text: Lacking hope, Hamlet abandons boundaries when wearing frock

indicators.note: Hamlet's remains wear the frock, so they go inside it

parts.note: a frock is a dress

indicators.note: the name loses its outer letters, the boundaries at each end

explanation.surface: A despairing Hamlet sheds all restraint and puts on a dress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandons boundaries' strips the first and last letters from the name; 'when wearing' means those inner letters go inside the frock.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreamless means without dreams, taken here as without aspirations or hopes.

clue.text: Begin making a move forward to get upgrade

indicators.note: the letter A is moved along the word, further into it

parts.note: to arise is to begin or come into being

explanation.surface: An instruction to start progressing in order to be promoted.
explanation.walkthrough: The A of ARISE shifts one place along to make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise something is to lift it to a higher level, the same idea as upgrade.

clue.text: Awareness of life, for example, when one is inside

indicators.note: the letter for one is inside the other piece

parts.note: life imprisonment is one example of a prison sentence
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Consciousness of being alive, as experienced while someone is in prison.
explanation.definitionFit: Sentience is the capacity to feel and perceive, a basic kind of consciousness.

clue.text: Hotel boss going crazy to find mass supplier

parts.note: Hotel is H in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: crazy says the letters of the two words go wild into a new order

explanation.surface: A hotel manager goes mad looking for a wholesale vendor.
explanation.definitionFit: The Higgs boson is the particle tied to the field that gives other particles their mass.

clue.text: Staple item on the early bird menu?

definitions.text: Staple item on the early bird menu?

parts.words: Staple item on the early bird menu?
parts.note: from the proverb that the early bird catches it: an early-rising bird's regular food

explanation.walkthrough: An 'early bird menu' sounds like a cheap restaurant deal, but it is a real bird's diet.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds eat earthworms, and the proverb says the early bird catches one.

clue.text: Cleaners, underworked, having coffee outside

indicators.note: the coffee goes outside the other piece, so it surrounds it

parts.note: a latte is a milky coffee
read as under worked: the word under, worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Overstretched cleaning staff take a coffee break outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'underworked' looks like a description of the cleaners but splits as 'under' plus 'worked', an anagram signal; 'outside' puts the coffee round the result.
explanation.definitionFit: A launderette washes clothes, so it is a place of cleaners in the sense of a cleaning business.

clue.text: Very little in Catholic teaching initially was read during troubles

indicators.note: the small amount goes in the abbreviation

parts.note: RC stands for Roman Catholic
an iota is a tiny amount

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Catholic doctrine was barely glanced at during a period of unrest.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a description: the Riot Act was the British law read aloud to disperse a rioting crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: Officials historically recited the Riot Act's proclamation to a disorderly mob before force could be used.

clue.text: They make good stuff that keeps theatre ventilated

indicators.note: the fabric keeps, or holds, the other letters inside

parts.note: rep is a ribbed fabric, and stuff is an old word for fabric
to air a room is to ventilate it
ER, the emergency room, is the hospital theatre for urgent cases

explanation.surface: Fabric that keeps a playhouse airy is something they make well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'They make good' means they mend; AIRER goes inside REPS.
explanation.definitionFit: Repairers mend broken things, and to make good is to put damage right.

clue.text: One brought in to launch vessel into river

indicators.note: the vessel is put into the river

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland
a raft is a simple floating craft

explanation.surface: Someone is recruited to push a boat out on to a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A draftee is a conscript, someone drafted into the armed forces.

clue.text: In disarray, hunts made opposing camps

indicators.note: disarray means disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Chaotic hunts created two rival sides.
explanation.definitionFit: Us and them describes two opposed groups who see each other as outsiders.

clue.text: Strip where waste left rotting

parts.note: pee is bodily waste
food that has gone off is rotting

explanation.surface: A strip of land where rubbish has been left to decay.
explanation.definitionFit: To peel off is to remove clothes or a layer, as in stripping.

clue.text: Simple angle concealing facilities getting erected

indicators.note: the angling word conceals the other piece inside it

parts.note: to angle is to fish

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting something upright reads it from bottom to top, i.e. backwards

parts.note: the loo is the toilet, often called the facilities

explanation.surface: A plain angle hides a set of toilets being put up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting erected' in a down clue means the toilet word is read upwards; 'concealing' puts it inside the angling word.
explanation.definitionFit: Simple can mean foolish or slow-witted.

clue.text: Standards of those who stop things happening

explanation.surface: Flags belonging to people who prohibit things.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard is a flag or ensign, and a banner is too; banners also prohibit things.

clue.text: Encourage support for British boom

indicators.note: in a down answer the supporting piece sits beneath what it holds up

parts.note: to urge on is to encourage

explanation.surface: Campaigners urge backing for a British economic upturn.
explanation.definitionFit: To burgeon is to grow rapidly and flourish, as an economy does in a boom.

clue.text: For a short distance, they precede Jodi's characters

definitions.meaning: each of ... comes just before J, O, D, I in the alphabet

explanation.surface: Briefly, someone's name is introduced by these.
explanation.walkthrough: Shift each letter of JODI back one place in the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: An inch is about two and a half centimetres, a tiny length.

clue.text: Watercourse constructed initially from the bottom

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of the word before it

parts.note: anal relates to the bottom, the backside

explanation.surface: A waterway built up from the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A canal is a man-made channel for water, a kind of watercourse.

clue.text: Don't hold it, because it won't happen (unless you're underwater)

definitions.text: Don't hold it, because it won't happen (unless you're underwater)

parts.words: Don't hold it, because it won't happen (unless you're underwater)
parts.note: the idiom tells people not to wait for something unlikely; holding the thing literally is for swimmers

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'don't hold ___' means don't expect it; the bracket adds the literal reading for swimmers and divers.
explanation.definitionFit: Don't hold your breath is an idiom urging someone not to wait expectantly for an unlikely event.

clue.text: Composer broadcast towering study

indicators.note: broadcast signals words spoken out over the air

parts.note: a high den: a tall room for study

explanation.surface: A musician's work is aired from a lofty study.
explanation.definitionFit: Joseph Haydn was an Austrian classical composer of symphonies and string quartets.

clue.text: Posh set contains odd characters seeking attention

indicators.note: the first, third, fifth and seventh letters of the two words are taken

explanation.surface: A smart crowd includes some eccentrics who want to be noticed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contains' is a link here: the odd letters of 'Posh set' read straight through.
explanation.definitionFit: Psst is the hissed sound used to catch someone's attention quietly.

clue.text: Female makes part of her nest in elms

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A female bird builds her nest in the elm trees.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernestine is a woman's given name, so it stands for a female.

clue.text: Creep sending daughter back just now

indicators.note: the daughter's letter is sent back towards the start of the word

parts.note: a toady is a fawning creep

explanation.surface: A sycophant packs a girl off home right this minute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sending back' moves D one place earlier in TOADY.
explanation.definitionFit: Today can mean nowadays, at the present time.

clue.text: Divided heads of state patently lacking in trust

indicators.note: heads are the first letters of each of the following words

explanation.surface: Split leaders of a nation who clearly don't trust each other.
explanation.definitionFit: Split is a past participle meaning separated into parts, the same as divided.

clue.text: Freeloaders switching how clothes are stored

indicators.note: the two words of the phrase switch places

parts.note: clothes are kept on hangers in a wardrobe

explanation.surface: Spongers changing how they keep their clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: ON HANGERS becomes HANGERS ON when the words swap.
explanation.definitionFit: Hangers-on attach themselves to someone for benefit, living off them as freeloaders do.
